skill.name: shadcn-ui
skill.description: Guidance for building React interfaces with shadcn/ui components, including setup, component discovery, theming, migration, and validation workflows.
skill.summary: Guides shadcn/ui component setup, customization, migration, and validation for React applications.

security_audit.summary: Static analysis produced many alerts, but reviewed evidence shows markdown examples, relative documentation links, TypeScript annotations, and local verification commands. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, credential access, or hidden execution. The skill uses Bash, Write, web fetch, and shadcn tools for normal component setup, so install commands should remain explicit.

remediation.issue: Install commands use the moving @latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Document that agents should ask before running shadcn CLI commands and allow pinned versions for controlled environments.

remediation.issue: Verification script searches the current project tree.
remediation.suggestion: Keep it opt-in, and state that it reads local config and package files only.
Add short notes that command snippets are documentation and not automatic execution steps.

content.value_statement: Modern React teams need consistent shadcn/ui components without repeated setup research. This skill guides component selection, installation, theming, migration, and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains shadcn/ui setup for new and existing React projects.
Guides component discovery with shadcn MCP tools and registry workflows.
Provides theming, typography, variant, and wrapper component patterns.
Shows form, authentication, and data table implementation examples.
Covers migration guidance from common React UI libraries.
Includes an optional shell script for local setup validation.
limitations: It does not audit third-party npm package contents.
It cannot guarantee that external shadcn documentation is current.
Generated examples still need project-specific testing and review.
CLI commands may modify files and install dependencies.

use_cases.title: Add Components to a React App
use_cases.description: Install and adapt shadcn/ui components while preserving Tailwind and project alias conventions.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Design System
use_cases.description: Create shared theme tokens, variants, and wrapper components around copied shadcn/ui source.

use_cases.title: Migrate from Another UI Kit
use_cases.description: Plan phased replacement of Material UI, Chakra UI, or Ant Design components with shadcn/ui patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a shadcn/ui Button to my React project. Explain the install step, imports, and a simple usage pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up an Existing App
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my project setup for shadcn/ui. Check Tailwind, components.json, aliases, and the cn utility before adding components.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Theme and Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan to customize shadcn/ui colors, typography, and button variants. Keep accessibility and dark mode support intact.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a UI Library Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my current component library with shadcn/ui. Map replacements, migration order, risks, and validation checks for a staged rollout.

output_examples.input: User asks for a login form using shadcn/ui.
output: Recommended components for tabs, cards, inputs, labels, and buttons.
Installation sequence and file placement guidance.
Accessibility and validation checks before commit.

output_examples.input: User asks to customize the application theme.
output: Theme token checklist for light and dark modes.
Variant planning for buttons, forms, and layout components.
Review steps for contrast, typography, and responsive behavior.

output_examples.input: User asks to migrate from Chakra UI to shadcn/ui.
output: Component mapping from existing primitives to shadcn/ui equivalents.
Incremental rollout plan by screen risk and dependency depth.
Testing checklist for forms, modals, keyboard use, and visual parity.

best_practices: Use the shadcn CLI for standard components, then review the copied source before committing.
Keep accessibility behavior, ARIA attributes, keyboard support, and focus indicators when customizing components.
Run type checks, linting, visual review, and accessibility checks after component changes.
anti_patterns: Do not install large component sets before deciding which screens need them.
Do not overwrite custom component changes without reviewing upstream diffs.
Do not remove Radix or Base UI behavior to solve styling issues quickly.

faq.question: Does this skill install shadcn/ui automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the workflow and may suggest CLI commands that should be confirmed before running.

faq.question: Can it work with Next.js and Vite?
faq.answer: Yes. The guides cover common React setups, including Next.js and Vite style project structures.

faq.question: Does it support custom registries?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains shadcn registry discovery tools and custom registry workflows from components.json.

faq.question: Will it maintain accessibility?
faq.answer: It emphasizes keeping ARIA, keyboard behavior, focus handling, and disabled states during customization.

faq.question: Can it migrate an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides migration planning and component mapping, but teams still need staged review.

faq.question: Does it replace official shadcn/ui documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes practical workflows and examples, while official docs remain the source of truth.
